touches.text: `cairn help` lists [all], then [operator], then [cairn], then every other device in alphabetical order, because `cairn` itself is special. Help is called, returns its results, and is done. Help at any other level looks in the bin folders inside that device's tree for the shortcuts relevant to the input. (Akien, 2026-11-05)

[all] is the verbs every device answers because the basemost shim defines them — help among them; stop, pause, or a future `pid` (the pids a device owns) would be [all] verbs too. So [all] is read from the base shim's verb table, never listed by hand. (Q, open-ae78c6e4700d, Akien 2026-11-05)

help is asked from anywhere, so it is everywhere and defined once: a root verb in the base shim that answers exactly as `list` does — `help` is the word people will type, `list` the system's. `list` carries the device's bin shortcuts beside its verbs and views, readable cold (no bus, no device woken), so `cairn help` answers when nothing else is up. ("help can just call list. help is specifically an anticipation of the behavior of the other monkeys in my species." Akien 2026-11-05)
help - the verb list with help strings; always human readable
list - enumerates verbs, views and panes, any list of things that might be published; returns json (show list <foo> formats it for humans)

Every verb anywhere is reached from the cairn command, as a path: cairn <device> [<machine> ...] <verb>. No central list: help at any level prints that level's own verbs under [<name>], alpha order, then calls back up the tree to its parent, which does the same, out to [cairn]. The groups come out flat, one after another, not nested: cairn codemother inspector_gadget help  -> [inspector_gadget] ... then [codemother] ... then [cairn] ... A device may ask another device help over the bus the same way; nothing being built needs that yet. (Q#2, Akien 2026-11-03)

Any device or machine may have a bin/ beside its code (cairn/devices/<device>/bin/, .../machines/<machine>/bin/). That folder IS its list of shortcuts: add a file to add one, delete it to remove one. A shortcut is just a script that calls the long form, which also saves the walk from searching farther (eg `cairn superclaude` → `cairn cc superclaude`; `cairn show temp` → `cairn recovery show temp`), or does work itself (eg initialization, install). Shortcuts can go anywhere, beside what they serve (RULE 1).

Repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher itself (cairn, cairn.cmd), the one thing on PATH, so it runs even when the package won't import (5.3.2.7). Every shortcut lives in the bin/ of the device or machine it belongs to. Its bin/ plus its bus verbs is what help lists at that level (2.4.11). (Q#12: Akien let CC choose, 2026-11-03; CC kept his walk.)
base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external.
